newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seeks to expand empowerment zones program.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seeks to expand empowerment zones program.

text.p: President Clinton Thursday urged Congress to expand in three ways the administration's four-year-old program aimed at stimulating economic growth in poor urban and rural areas nationwide.
The proposal would build on an administration program launched in 1993 that provides business tax incentives in nine federally designated "empowerment zones" and 95 "enterprise communities."

Clinton today proposed that Congress loosen some current restrictions on tax-exempt financing in zones and communities and designate another 20 empowerment zones and 80 enterprise communities nationwide.

Of the 20 new empowerment zones, 15 would be in urban areas and five in rural areas, the budget proposal said. Fifty of the 80 new enterprise communities would be urban and 30 would be rural, according to the proposal.
Under the President's plan, businesses in the new enterprise communities would be eligible for tax-exempt financing and tax incentives currently authorized for "brownfield" sites.
Brownfields are land parcels that are lightly contaminated by previous industrial use but do not pose serious enough health risks to qualify for federal Superfund financing.

Eligible businesses also would no longer be subject to state caps on the volume of specialized muni financing that they can do. Rather, they would be subject only to zone-by-zone caps, the proposal said.
The federal government would have to make the new designations, which would last for 10 years, before 1999, the budget plan stated.
